WI:SCI.PS1.A.2.cc_advanced: I can choose the best material for a purpose by testing its properties and explain my choice.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that substances have different observable properties suited to different purposes and that objects can be built from smaller parts.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.2.cc_approaching: I can describe a material as hard, soft, rough, or smooth, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.2.cc_emerging: I can sort objects by what they are made of, with help.

WI:SCI.PS1.A.5.cc_advanced: I can use measurements of several properties to identify an unknown material and explain conservation of matter.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that matter is made of particles too small to see, is always conserved, and can be identified by measuring properties.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.5.cc_approaching: I can measure a property such as mass or magnetism to help identify a material, with support.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.5.cc_emerging: I can say that sugar seems to disappear in water but is still there.

WI:SCI.PS1.A.m.cc_advanced: I can use an atomic model to explain a property, phase change, and conservation of matter in one example.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.m.cc_at_target: I can use the idea that matter is made of atoms and molecules to explain properties, states of matter, phase changes, and conservation.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe particles in solids, liquids, and gases, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of tiny particles.

WI:SCI.PS1.A.h.cc_advanced: I can use atomic structure and periodic patterns to predict and explain the behavior of matter in a new reaction.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.h.cc_at_target: I can use the sub-atomic model and electric charge interactions to explain matter's structure, reactions, and periodic table patterns.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe protons, neutrons, and electrons and find valence electrons, with a periodic table.
WI:SCI.PS1.A.h.cc_emerging: I can name the parts of an atom, using a model.

WI:SCI.PS1.B.2.cc_advanced: I can predict whether a change from heating or cooling can be reversed and test my prediction.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that heating or cooling can cause observable changes and that some changes can be reversed and some cannot.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.2.cc_approaching: I can sort changes, such as melting ice and cooking an egg, into reversible and not reversible, with help.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.2.cc_emerging: I can say that ice melts when it gets warm.

WI:SCI.PS1.B.5.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation to show a new substance forms and that total mass stays the same.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that mixing substances can make new substances with different properties and that total mass stays the same.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.5.cc_approaching: I can describe signs that a new substance formed after mixing, with support.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.5.cc_emerging: I can observe changes when two substances are mixed.

WI:SCI.PS1.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use a model to show atoms rearranging in a reaction and explain why it releases or absorbs energy.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that reacting substances rearrange into new molecules, atoms are conserved, and reactions release or absorb energy.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.m.cc_approaching: I can count atoms before and after a reaction model, with support.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that chemical reactions make new substances.

WI:SCI.PS1.B.h.cc_advanced: I can predict reaction outcomes and rates using collision theory, atomic rearrangement, and energy changes.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain chemical processes in terms of molecular collisions, rearrangement of atoms, and energy changes.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how collisions between particles lead to reactions, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS1.B.h.cc_emerging: I can identify reactants and products in an equation.

WI:SCI.PS1.C.h.cc_advanced: I can compare fusion, fission, and decay and calculate or explain the energy involved in each.
WI:SCI.PS1.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that nuclear processes such as fusion, fission, and radioactive decay release or absorb energy.
WI:SCI.PS1.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe the difference between fission and fusion, using diagrams.
WI:SCI.PS1.C.h.cc_emerging: I can say that the nucleus is in the center of an atom.

WI:SCI.PS2.A.K.cc_advanced: I can predict how a stronger or weaker push will change an object's motion and test it.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that pushes and pulls have different strengths and directions and can start, stop, or change an object's motion.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.K.cc_approaching: I can show a push and a pull and say what happened to the object, with help.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.K.cc_emerging: I can push or pull a toy to make it move.

WI:SCI.PS2.A.3.cc_advanced: I can use patterns of motion to predict future motion and explain the effect of unbalanced forces.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.3.cc_at_target: I can describe motion by size and direction, explain that unbalanced forces change motion, and use patterns to predict motion.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.3.cc_approaching: I can identify balanced and unbalanced forces in a picture, with support.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.3.cc_emerging: I can say which way an object moves when pushed.

WI:SCI.PS2.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how force and mass together change an object's speed, velocity, or acceleration, with examples.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.m.cc_at_target: I can describe motion using speed, velocity, and acceleration and account for the role of mass in changes of motion.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.m.cc_approaching: I can calculate speed from distance and time, with a worked example.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say whether an object is speeding up or slowing down.

WI:SCI.PS2.A.h.cc_advanced: I can use F = ma and momentum to analyze and predict motion in a complex situation.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.h.cc_at_target: I can describe motion quantitatively and use Newton's second law and conservation of momentum to predict changes.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.h.cc_approaching: I can use F = ma or p = mv to solve a simple problem, with support.
WI:SCI.PS2.A.h.cc_emerging: I can define speed, velocity, and acceleration, with a word bank.

WI:SCI.PS2.B.K.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain what will happen when two objects collide.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that when objects touch or collide they push on each other and can change motion.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.K.cc_approaching: I can show what happens when one ball hits another, with help.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.K.cc_emerging: I can roll a ball to hit another object.

WI:SCI.PS2.B.3.cc_advanced: I can design a test to compare contact and non-contact forces and explain the results.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that some forces act through contact and some, like magnetic and electric forces, act without touching.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.3.cc_approaching: I can show a magnet moving an object without touching it, with support.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.3.cc_emerging: I can say that magnets pull some objects.

WI:SCI.PS2.B.5.cc_advanced: I can explain why objects fall toward Earth's center everywhere on the planet, using a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's gravity pulls objects near its surface toward the planet's center.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.5.cc_approaching: I can show that dropped objects fall down, with sentence frames.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.5.cc_emerging: I can say that things fall to the ground.

WI:SCI.PS2.B.m.cc_advanced: I can map a field and explain how its strength changes with distance.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that forces acting at a distance involve fields that can be mapped by their strength and effect.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.m.cc_approaching: I can use iron filings or a compass to show a magnetic field, with support.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that magnets can push or pull without touching.

WI:SCI.PS2.B.h.cc_advanced: I can use field models to explain and predict how electric and magnetic forces and energy change with distance.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that forces at a distance are described by fields that transfer energy and depend on the objects and distance.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how distance affects gravitational or electric force, with support.
WI:SCI.PS2.B.h.cc_emerging: I can name forces that act at a distance.

WI:SCI.PS3.A.4.cc_advanced: I can design a test to show that faster objects have more energy and explain my evidence.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that moving objects have energy and faster objects have more energy.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.4.cc_approaching: I can compare two moving objects and say which has more energy, with help.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.4.cc_emerging: I can say that moving things have energy.

WI:SCI.PS3.A.m.cc_advanced: I can identify kinetic and several forms of potential energy in a system and explain how they change.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.m.cc_at_target: I can distinguish kinetic energy from the different forms of potential energy.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.m.cc_approaching: I can sort examples into kinetic or potential energy, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.m.cc_emerging: I can name kinetic and potential energy.

WI:SCI.PS3.A.h.cc_advanced: I can explain with examples why systems move toward more stable, lower energy states.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that systems move toward more stable states.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.h.cc_approaching: I can give an example of a system becoming more stable, such as a ball rolling downhill, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that a ball rolls down and stops.

WI:SCI.PS3.B.4.cc_advanced: I can build a device that converts energy and explain each transfer and conversion.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy moves by moving objects, sound, light, or electric currents and can change from one form to another.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.4.cc_approaching: I can name ways energy moves, such as light and sound, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.4.cc_emerging: I can say that a lamp gives light.

WI:SCI.PS3.B.m.cc_advanced: I can track energy changes in a process and explain how temperature relates to total energy for different materials.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.m.cc_at_target: I can track energy changes in physical and chemical interactions and explain how temperature and total energy depend on matter.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.m.cc_approaching: I can describe an energy transfer in a simple system, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that heat moves from hot to cold.

WI:SCI.PS3.B.h.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy in a system and predict transfers using motion and configuration energy.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy is conserved in a system and describe transfers using energy of motion and position of particles.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.h.cc_approaching: I can complete an energy bar chart for a simple system, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that energy is not created or destroyed.

WI:SCI.PS3.C.K.cc_advanced: I can test and explain how changing push strength changes motion or shape.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that bigger pushes and pulls cause bigger changes in motion or shape.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.K.cc_approaching: I can compare a big and small push and what happened, with help.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.K.cc_emerging: I can push a toy hard and soft.

WI:SCI.PS3.C.4.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain energy transfer in collisions of different speeds.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that in collisions, contact forces transfer energy and change objects' motions.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.4.cc_approaching: I can describe what happens to two objects after they collide, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.4.cc_emerging: I can observe two objects bumping into each other.

WI:SCI.PS3.C.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how forces transfer energy in a real interaction and predict the outcome.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that interacting objects exert forces on each other that can transfer energy between them.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.m.cc_approaching: I can describe the forces and energy change when two objects interact, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say that objects push on each other when they touch.

WI:SCI.PS3.C.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how changing the arrangement of objects in a field changes the stored energy, with calculations.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that fields contain energy that depends on the arrangement of objects in the field.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how moving magnets closer changes stored energy, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.C.h.cc_emerging: I can name gravitational, electric, and magnetic fields.

WI:SCI.PS3.D.K.cc_advanced: I can compare how sunlight warms different surfaces and explain my results.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that sunlight warms Earth's surface.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.K.cc_approaching: I can feel and compare a surface in sun and shade, with help.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.K.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun makes things warm.

WI:SCI.PS3.D.5.cc_advanced: I can trace energy from the sun into plants and food or fuel and explain how it is released.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants capture energy from sunlight for food or fuel and that stored energy can be converted to useful energy.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.5.cc_approaching: I can describe that food energy comes from plants and the sun, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.5.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight.

WI:SCI.PS3.D.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy stored in sugar by photosynthesis is released by respiration or combustion.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants store sunlight energy in sugars and that this energy is released by respiration or combustion.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.m.cc_approaching: I can describe the energy changes in photosynthesis, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.m.cc_emerging: I can say that plants store energy from the sun.

WI:SCI.PS3.D.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how photosynthesis captures solar energy and why energy becomes less useful in each transfer.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that photosynthesis captures the sun's radiation and that energy is converted to less useful forms but not destroyed.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy changes form in photosynthesis, with support.
WI:SCI.PS3.D.h.cc_emerging: I can say that plants capture the sun's energy.

WI:SCI.PS4.A.1.cc_advanced: I can show that sound makes things vibrate and vibrations make sound, and explain my evidence.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that sound can make matter vibrate and vibrating matter can make sound.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.1.cc_approaching: I can feel a vibration when I make a sound, with help.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.1.cc_emerging: I can make sounds with objects.

WI:SCI.PS4.A.4.cc_advanced: I can make waves with different amplitudes and wavelengths and explain how waves can move objects.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that waves are regular patterns of motion that differ in amplitude and wavelength and can move objects.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.4.cc_approaching: I can label the amplitude and wavelength of a wave, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.4.cc_emerging: I can make a wave in water.

WI:SCI.PS4.A.m.cc_advanced: I can use a wave model to explain sound and light phenomena and how waves transmit energy.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.m.cc_at_target: I can describe a wave model with wavelength, frequency, and amplitude and explain that mechanical waves need a medium.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.m.cc_approaching: I can label parts of a wave and say that sound needs a medium, with support.

WI:SCI.PS4.A.h.cc_advanced: I can calculate wave properties in different media and explain how waves carry information and energy.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that wavelength and frequency are related by wave speed, which depends on the wave and medium.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.h.cc_approaching: I can use v = f x wavelength with given values, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.A.h.cc_emerging: I can define wavelength and frequency.

WI:SCI.PS4.B.1.cc_advanced: I can test which objects can be seen in different light conditions and explain the results.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that objects can be seen only when there is light to illuminate them.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.1.cc_approaching: I can show that I cannot see in a dark box until light shines in, with help.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.1.cc_emerging: I can say that we need light to see.

WI:SCI.PS4.B.4.cc_advanced: I can model how light reflects from objects into the eye and explain how mirrors work.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that we see objects when light reflected from them enters our eyes.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.4.cc_approaching: I can draw arrows to show light going from an object to my eye, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.4.cc_emerging: I can say that eyes need light to see.

WI:SCI.PS4.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use a wave model to predict how light will reflect, refract, or be absorbed by different objects.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.m.cc_at_target: I can use a wave model to explain how light interacts with objects.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.m.cc_approaching: I can describe reflection and absorption of light, with a diagram.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that light can bounce off objects.

WI:SCI.PS4.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain when a wave model or photon model better explains electromagnetic radiation and its uses.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that wave and photon models both explain features and applications of electromagnetic radiation.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.h.cc_approaching: I can name types of electromagnetic radiation and a use for each, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that light is a type of electromagnetic radiation.

WI:SCI.PS4.C.1.cc_advanced: I can design a device to send a message over a distance and explain how it works.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.1.cc_at_target: I can explain that people use devices to send and receive information.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.1.cc_approaching: I can name devices that send messages, such as phones, with help.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.1.cc_emerging: I can show how I can send a message by waving or calling.

WI:SCI.PS4.C.4.cc_advanced: I can create my own code to send and decode a message and compare it with others.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that patterns can encode, send, receive, and decode information.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.4.cc_approaching: I can use a given code, such as Morse code, to send a message, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.4.cc_emerging: I can follow a simple pattern of sounds or lights.

WI:SCI.PS4.C.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how a digital signal of 1s and 0s is sent by waves and why it is reliable.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that waves can transmit digital information made of patterns of 1s and 0s.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.m.cc_approaching: I can show how a message can be written as 1s and 0s, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.m.cc_emerging: I can name devices that use digital information.

WI:SCI.PS4.C.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how digitization allows large amounts of information to be stored and shared, including its risks.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that large amounts of information can be stored and shipped because it is digitized.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one advantage of digital storage, with support.
WI:SCI.PS4.C.h.cc_emerging: I can name ways we store digital information.
